name: Grey Good
life: “I ran shifts through a winter when the whole family lived in two rooms.” Sunday often includes a stop at the downtown fountain, where Grey keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I papered over the wall because my boy never reached his next mark. His sister wants hers back.
appearance: Grey has full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side. Look for a neat white crop. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a brown corduroy jacket with one cuff folded back twice. In conversation Grey counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Grey can be lavish with time and quite careful with cash. A free afternoon is sometimes the biggest gift Grey can afford to give, and family knows to take it seriously.
agenda: To give the surviving daughter back the marks she remembers.
family: Keiko Ruiz is Grey’s half-sibling. Grey brings a spare shopping bag. Keiko chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *Midnight cinnamon*, Keiko says, “I have the recipe nobody else remembers. It calls for leaving one bun on a lonely neighbor's step.”
connections: Vera Hardy. The decision about uncovering a dead child's mark needs the tenant, as well as the landlord, in the room. Also in the story is Sam Collins (trace maker).

reactions.situation: A family asks for a tracing to take away
reactions.response: Grey asks which pencil marks the family recognizes as their own.

reactions.situation: Someone offers a cash reward for naming a rumored culprit
reactions.response: Grey asks what evidence supports the accusation and declines to supply a name on gossip alone.

reactions.situation: If invited to an expensive outing
reactions.response: Grey suggests meeting afterward and explains why without asking the others to abandon their plans.
